chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Yaqub ibn Shu'ayb, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said to him, 'I give the man twenty dinars for his fruit, on the condition that I say to him: When your fruit is established for any amount, it is mine for that price. If you are pleased, I will take it, and if you dislike, I will leave it.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'You have no leeway to give him [the money] and not stipulate anything.' I said, 'May I be your ransom, he does not name a specific amount, and Allah knows that is from his intention.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'It is not correct if that is from his intention.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling fruit for a price to be named by the seller later?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the ruling on conditional fruit sales (mu'atah) by rejecting the validity of a fixed price with an unstipulated final amount, even if the seller's intention is known. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) emphasizes that for the contract to be valid, the price must be explicitly determined or stipulated at the time of the agreement to eliminate gharar (uncertainty). This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on contractual clarity and the prevention of dispute in commercial transactions.
